title: Pulled Pork Wrap (Freezer Meal Prep)
description: Burrito-style wrap for work lunches: Joe's pulled pork, Fiesta blend cheese, and homemade cowboy candy in a Mission burrito-size tortilla. Seared shut in a skillet, frozen, then microwaved at work.

ingredients.note: Joe's Slow Cooker Pulled Pork (d5b95a0f8164). Drain off the juice and cool it before filling. If it's frozen, thaw it in the fridge first.
per wrap. Lighter than the 2/3 cup in a quesadilla. Use less for cheese-light.
Canned Cowboy Candy (80/20 Jalapeno and Habanero) (5e18b57fd262). Go up to 2 tbsp if you want more heat.

steps: Drain the pork well and let it cool. Hot, wet filling steams the tortilla and makes it soggy in the freezer.
Warm the tortillas so they fold without cracking: wrap them in a barely damp towel and microwave about 1 minute.
Lay a tortilla flat. Put the cheese in a strip just below the center, then the pork on top of it, then the cowboy candy.
Fold the bottom up over the filling, tuck in both sides, and roll it up tight so the seam ends up on the bottom.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium with a little oil or spray. Set the wraps in seam side down and cook 1 to 2 minutes, until golden and sealed. Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more.
Cool the wraps completely on a rack. Wrapping them warm traps steam, which makes them soggy and causes freezer burn.
Wrap each one tightly in plastic wrap or foil, put them in a freezer bag, label with the date, and freeze.
At work: take off the foil or plastic, wrap the wrap in a damp paper towel, and set it on a plate. Microwave 2 minutes, flip, then microwave 2 minutes more.
Check the center with a thermometer. It needs to reach 165F. If it doesn't, add 30 to 60 seconds at a time. Let it rest 1 minute before eating.
source: Recipe Keeper for Joe, Oct 24, 2026 (Joe chose the ingredients; Recipe Keeper worked out the portions and method). Portions guided by Baking Mischief freezer burritos https://bakingmischief.com/freezer-burritos/ and Feel Good Foodie https://feelgoodfoodie.net/recipe/breakfast-burrito/ . Sear-to-seal, cooling, and freezing method from Feel Good Foodie. Microwave reheat from America's Test Kitchen https://www.americastestkitchen.com/articles/6029-how-to-reheat-frozen-breakfast-burritos and Baking Mischief. 165F, thawing, and refreezing from USDA FSIS https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/leftovers-and-food-safety . Mission burrito size is 10 inch: https://www.missionfoods.com/products/burrito-flour-tortillas/
notes:
Not yet made by Joe. These are starting portions and times to adjust after the first batch.
Portions: 3/4 cup pork, 1/3 cup cheese, and 1 tbsp cowboy candy is about 1 1/4 cups of filling. Sources put a 10 inch burrito at about 1 to 1 1/2 cups of filling (Baking Mischief uses 1/2 cup meat and 1/4 cup cheese plus rice; Feel Good Foodie says to stay around 1 1/2 cups so it closes). Joe's bowls use about 1 cup of protein and his quesadilla uses 2/3 cup cheese. The pork and cowboy candy are both already spicy, so start with 1 tbsp of the 80/20 cowboy candy.
Sear: 1 to 2 min per side over medium (Feel Good Foodie's seam-side-down sear). This seals the wrap. The filling is cool, so the cheese may not fully melt until you reheat it.
Freezer life: best within about 1 month for tortilla texture (Baking Mischief), good up to 2 to 3 months (Feel Good Foodie). USDA says frozen leftovers keep 3 to 4 months for quality.
Reheat: ATK says 2 to 4 min in a damp paper towel. Baking Mischief says 4 to 5 min, flipping halfway. Work microwaves vary in power, so check for 165F (USDA) in the center on the first one.
Pork safety: USDA says leftovers thawed in the fridge can be refrozen without reheating. Use thawed pork within 3 to 4 days. Don't make wraps with pork thawed on the counter.
Cheese-light: cut the cheese to 1/4 cup or less. The wrap still seals without it.

healthy: Pulled pork gives a lot of protein.
Portioned and homemade, so it beats a fast-food lunch.
No rice or beans, so there's less starch than a typical burrito.
not_healthy: Large flour tortilla is refined carbs.
Pork butt and cheese add saturated fat and sodium.
